name: claw-control-ui
description: First-class monorepo root for the Chela clients: core (shared rules), desktop (Electron), mobile (iOS). No platform is the root; each is a peer.
author: Abi Renhart

scripts.//: Root scripts fan out to every platform, no platform privileged. JS platforms (core, desktop) run through pnpm --recursive/--filter; mobile is Swift and runs through its own tooling in scripts/mobile.mjs. lint fans out in PARALLEL (it is cheap). test runs the JS packages RECURSIVELY (pnpm's default is one package at a time): the desktop suite has CPU-timing-sensitive tests that flake when core and desktop test processes contend for cores on a small box, and CI runs each platform on its own runner anyway, so parallel test buys nothing and costs reliability. Mobile runs after the JS half in each case, and a mobile failure does not mask a JS failure or vice versa.
scripts.test: pnpm run --recursive --if-present test && pnpm run test:mobile
scripts.lint: pnpm run --parallel --recursive --if-present --aggregate-output lint && pnpm run lint:mobile
scripts.build: pnpm run build:desktop && pnpm run build:mobile
scripts.//gates: The two .githooks run these instead of cd-ing into desktop/ and reaching for its scripts directly. The GUI boot smoke and the page measurements need a real desktop session, so they stay desktop-specific work, but they are reached through a ROOT script now: the hook lives at the repo root and calls the root, which is what makes no platform the root.
scripts.hooks:install: git config core.hooksPath "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.githooks" && echo "hooks installed: core.hooksPath -> .githooks"
